decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.

changes.quote: Recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity has slowed from its strong pace in the third quarter.
changes.explanation: The Fed acknowledges that economic growth has cooled off compared to the very strong third quarter.

changes.quote: Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated.
changes.explanation: The Committee recognizes that price pressures have improved over the last year, though inflation is still higher than their target.

tone_quotes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 21.19% APR costs about $88.29 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.04% and moved -16 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 7.22% would fall by about $32.42 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 3.7%, and employers added an average of 147k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 3.1% over the past year (November 2023); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 3.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 4.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -27 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 1.37%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.39% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will continue watching incoming economic data to determine if any further policy changes are needed. An educational forecast model suggests the next meeting has a 70% chance of a hold, a 29% chance of a cut, and a 1% chance of a hike.
